record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: Let G^1_μ(D²) be the C¹ compactly supported Lebesgue-measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of the disk. Does every C¹-neighborhood of the identity in G^1_μ(D²) contain some map g with positive metric entropy h_μ(g) > 0?

evidence.quote: For every C1-neighbourhood W of the identity in G1μ there exists g ∈ W such that hμ(g) > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ denote the closed unit disk, equipped with the Lebesgue area measure $\mu$. Let $G^1_\mu(D^2)$ denote the group of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms of $D^2$ that preserve $\mu$ and are compactly supported in the interior of $D^2$, endowed with the $C^1$ topology. For a $\mu$-preserving diffeomorphism $g$, let $h_\mu(g)$ denote its metric (measure-theoretic) entropy with respect to $\mu$.

Question: Does every $C^1$-neighborhood of the identity in $G^1_\mu(D^2)$ contain at least one diffeomorphism $g$ with $h_\mu(g) > 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is Herman's positive entropy conjecture. Berger and Turaev proved that in every neighborhood of the identity (in the C^∞ topology, hence also C^1) within the group of smooth area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the 2-disk, there exists a diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy. The problem is therefore solved in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: Berger and Turaev's proof of Herman's conjecture of positive entropy
status_evidence.snippet: In every neighbourhood of identity in the set of smooth symplectic diffeomorphisms of the 2-dimensional disc, there exists a diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Herman's positive-entropy-near-identity conjecture for the disk has been resolved positively by Berger and Turaev.

status_evidence.title: On Herman's positive entropy conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The identity map of the disk can be C∞-perturbed to a conservative diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy, proving a conjecture of Herman.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is established: arbitrarily small smooth area-preserving perturbations of the identity on the disk yield positive metric entropy.
